newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambian court set to rule on Chiluba's eligibility.
newsitem.headline: Zambian court set to rule on Chiluba's eligibility.

text.p: The Zambian Supreme Court will on Wednesday rule on a petition filed by opposition parties challenging President Frederick Chiluba's eligibility to contest elections set for November 18, court officials said on Tuesday.
Four opposition parties filed the petition to test Chiluba's credentials, alleging the president lied about his parentage and nationality in filing nomination papers for the elections.
The parties have also applied for a stay of the elections until a ruling has been made on the petition.

"The court has allowed an inter parte hearing of the injunction tomorrow. We expect it to rule on the injunction and, subsequently, on the petition, tomorrow (Wednesday)," court officials told reporters.

The petition was filed by former president Kenneth Kaunda's United National Independence Party (UNIP) and three smaller opposition parties after the adoption of constitutional clauses which ban first-generation Zambians standing for president.

The clauses are widely seen to be directed at Kaunda, whose parents were Malawian. They have been widely criticised by political observers and Western donor countries, which have cut or frozen aid to Zambia to force the government to reverse them.
The government, however, insists that the elections be held under the new laws.
President Chiluba's origins have been a source of much speculation in Zambia, with some newspapers and opposition parties claiming that he was born in Zaire.

The president's ambivalence about his roots has fuelled the debate. He has claimed at different times to have been born in the mining town of Kitwe and in a village in the northern Luapula Province which borders Zaire.
Chiluba travelled to Pretoria on Tuesday for a meeting with South African President Nelson Mandela, at which he is expected to discuss the controversy surrounding the elections.
